correctness.rationale: Every open interval cut by the finite named support is a transitive Aut(Q,<) stabilizer orbit; the stabilizer acts independently on different intervals. An invariant equivalence is either equality or universal inside each gap; any cross-orbit equivalence forces a whole gap to collapse, so all remaining choices are partitions of named points and collapsed gaps. This proves the Bell convolution with no missing cases. Least-support uniqueness for order atoms is established in Bojańczyk (2013), enabling inclusion-exclusion on supports. Dobinski moments give Bell log-convexity; termwise comparison yields F_k/F_{k-1}>=B_{k+1}/B_{k-1}; Grunwald–Serafin Bell ratio asymptotic yields O((log k)^2/k). The packaged checker independently enumerates finite partition proxies through k=3 and tests support essentiality through k=3, returning ALL_CHECKS_OK. Finite checks alone are not the infinite proof.
